blocks.x: I'll make a note that the date is February the 10th, I believe it is, it's 1962. And we're interviewing Mrs. Jeanette Kimball at her home. It's 2012 7th Street in New Artists. Do you mind giving your full name? And do you use the name Kimball yet?
Yes, Jeanette Salvat Kimball.
John Porter was the bass. He played tuba at that time.
And we had, let's see, I've mentioned the sax section, the trumpets, and the…
Trombones, I see.
The trombone was, I think it was still August Russo.
I never knew him, I guess. I think when we interviewed Louie Nelson, who said he'd played with them for… No, no, that was mixed up. Louie Barberin?
No, I'm mixed up.
That was the Sidney Desvinge band. Oh, yes. He was a big band.
No, Louie Barberin was our drummer then.
I was thinking trombones after Ridgely left. Do you remember who the trombones were?
Well, as I have foresaid, in the eight piece band we had Elvis Russo.
Oh, yes. Oh, that's right, sure.
Now, when we had the large band, we had Bill Matthews. Oh, Bill Matthews. Oh, sure. That's when he came. That's when he came in, in the big band. Yes, Bill Matthews.
And he stayed with him a long time then too.
He's one of the original members. Yes. Also, Louie Barberin and Narvin H. Kimball, we and myself.
I guess you all are about the last ones that are still…

We are the four original members. And a lot of them are dead and then some of them are in other groups. Other groups. For instance, Maya Kennedy and Clarence Hall is in Dave Bartholomew's band, but they are all original members also.
Yes, that's right.
And with the large band. And we played… We kept busy day and night.
Did you all do much traveling in those days?
We did quite a bit of traveling.
I know in late days they had that big bus that I know used to be over there in front of Mr. Barberin's home sometimes.
Yes, we had several buses and we used to do quite a lot of traveling all through the south. We didn't get east or north, but we went all through the south.

You know, at one time people have told me, I don't know if it's true, I better check, that they had… Celestan had two bands. One sort of his band would stay here and play and another one out on the road at times. Do you remember anything like that?
Well, if he did, it wasn't when I was with him. Not when you were with him? No.
Because… So I don't know if it's really true or somebody just told me that and then maybe they were confused about it. I don't know anything about it.
It wasn't at the time that I was with them. As I said, I stopped in 35 and then I didn't rejoin until 53. So it might have been during that period.
During that time. But it wasn't… Although he was out of the music business too during the war. He was for a while. I remember too when he broke his leg and all.
And when he reorganized, well then I didn't become a member of his band at that time. I was still out. But I didn't rejoin until 53. Yes.
That's funny, he used Octave Crosby, I guess, when he went in the paddock. Well, that was the time, yes. Yes.
And Mercedes also. Well, Mercedes too. She was with him. I've never heard of her. Yeah, she's very, very good. She was with him during that period also.
That's right, I've heard that but I never did know her. Yes.
And these fellas who I'm with now were with him at that period. Yes. Howard French and…
Yes, I remember those days. I heard them then.
John Thomas and that bunch. Eddie Pearson who was dead. They were all with him during that period. Yes, I remember. That was before I came in. Yes. And then when I came in, they all remained.

During that time, did you, I know you wouldn't have given up music, but did you play out in the public at all with any bands or by yourself or… Do you mean before I came to… No, in that period between 1935 when you were raising your family. Oh, yes.

Yes. I just wondered… I was with another band a while and then I played… Which band was if you don't mind? I was with Herbert Leary's orchestra for about five years during that time. And then I played solo at a nightclub, a colored nightclub. Where was that? Which? The Dew Drop.
Oh, yes, right over… I played over there.

And then I played, well we had a group too. We had a little group over there about six pieces. I played there about two years. So I was still in music, but I couldn't travel at that time. Therefore, I only played with bands who were stationary. Did you do much teaching?
You mentioned teaching your children… Well, I did.
I didn't do too much teaching over here because I just didn't have time. I was furthering my education and then I was rearing my children.

Did you take up regular… As I said, I don't want to try to get personal, I want to ask you all these questions so you don't have to ask… But did you go back to school, like to college or something? Or did you… Music, did you mean?
I furthered my education literarily as well as musically.
Yes, that's what I thought you meant that. I wasn't sure. And… It's nice to do that because a lot of people when they raise a family, they never think of…
Of course, I never did get my degree.
I had to stop.
I just didn't get it. But I still hope to. I don't feel that I'm too old. That's…
I know a lot of people keep on… Sometimes you read about some grandmother even that will get her college degree somewhere.

Because after my children started getting up some size, then I had to think about their education. Yes, that's right. And both of them have college degrees. So… Of which I'm very proud. But now that they are grown, well, I think about going back.
That would be nice if you have time. And the music doesn't keep people so busy nowadays like in the old days. It looks like it's not quite what it used to be.
And then I had so much on my hands with trying to rear a family. Yes. But… I've had quite a full life, of which I have enjoyed.
I see. When you rejoined the Celestan band, you were on the one record they made for Joe Merez's Southland, I know.
Oh, not when I first joined.
Weren't you? I mean after that. Quite some years after that. You know, the one that he has Marie Laveau and all of the…
Yes. And then I have been down there with Joe Merez on a lot of… with a lot of groups.
Other groups too. That's right. With Johnny St. Cyril, we have a lot of… Yes. Doc Suchon. And some of those groups.
I've been on quite a few sessions.
Maybe one of Jim Robinson or something. Yes, I know.
But we did make Marie Laveau with Papa's band for Joe Merez. Yes, I know. Golden Wedding, I think it's called.
Yes. With the big band, did they do any recording?

No, we didn't do any recording with the big band. We did the recording when we had the eight piece band. The eight piece band. And then in later years, after I rejoined Papa's house then, around 53, we made this record for Merez. But during the time that we had the 14 piece band, we didn't do any recording.
Is there anything else that you'd like to add about your life in music? Any advice that you'd have for any younger musicians coming up?

Well, it takes a lot of study, I can say that. But the young people don't want to study. That's right. They want to begin playing right away. But I still like that method of catechism and written work and all those sort of things. And when you're learning music. It has paid off for me. I wouldn't give anything for it. But of course the music pupils of today want to go right to the piano and begin playing. But how are you going to play if you don't know the basic things about music? So my advice would be to learn correctly. Have the right start. Anything that is done right where you can't help but make a success of it. But if you just try to run through something, you're going to lose something along the way. So I still believe in that written work and the catechism and the scales by all means. Because it gives dexterity. And I like sight reading, improvisation and things like that. Harmony. All of those things are essential. But they go in now for just playing. They don't care whether they have harmony or not. But I don't like that sort of playing. And as I said before, I owe everything to my first teacher.
And what is her name again now? Mrs. Stewart. What was her first name? Anna. Anna Stewart. And she's still living in New Orleans.
Yes, she's still living in New Orleans. Although she has retired. But she was a graduate of the Boston Conservatory. And she was wonderful.

I believe since I mentioned Louie Nelson, you know, there was a doctor, Nelson, who just died last summer, I guess. And his wife, who's been dead a long time, I never met her, also is a graduate in piano at Boston. She was. Music school in Boston, either New England or Boston Conservatory, I forget what. I was going to mention some of the musicians, even trumpet players and clarinetists, tell me that when they'd want to take up the instrument, their teacher, even people like Manuel Perez, before they'd teach it. . . .
